concepts.def: Caused by Earth's rotation on its axis.
Caused by the tilt of Earth's axis.
From the changing sunlit portion we see.
Solar and lunar eclipses from alignment of Sun, Earth, Moon.
Caused mainly by the Moon's gravity.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Lunar Disc & Eclipses — a core area of A-Level Astronomy.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Lunar Disc & Eclipses brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Lunar Disc & Eclipses.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Approximate length of a synodic month?
options: 27.3 days
29.5 days
30.0 days
31.0 days

mcqs.q: Phase when the lit side faces away from Earth?
options: Full Moon
New Moon
First quarter
Gibbous

mcqs.q: Why don't we have a solar eclipse at every new Moon?
options: The Earth moves into the Moon's shadow.
The Sun moves out of the way each month.
Because the Moon's orbit is tilted, so it usually passes above or below the Sun.
There is a solar eclipse every new Moon.
Exactly 30 days every time.
The roughly 29.5 days between one new Moon and the next.
The Earth moves into the Moon's shadow.
The time for one rotation of the Earth.

mcqs.q: During a lunar eclipse, what moves into shadow?
options: The time for one rotation of the Earth.
The Earth moves into the Moon's shadow.
The Moon moves into the Earth's shadow.
The Sun is blocked by the Moon.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Synodic month”?
options: Left half of the Moon (Northern Hemisphere) is lit, three weeks after New Moon.
Waxing = increasing lit fraction; waning = decreasing lit fraction.
Phase when the Moon is between Earth and the Sun; the lit side faces away from Earth.
Time between successive same phases (e.g., New Moon to New Moon): 29.5 days.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Last quarter”?
options: Time between successive same phases (e.g., New Moon to New Moon): 29.5 days.
Left half of the Moon (Northern Hemisphere) is lit, three weeks after New Moon.
Waxing = increasing lit fraction; waning = decreasing lit fraction.
Phase when the Moon is between Earth and the Sun; the lit side faces away from Earth.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Full Moon”?
options: Earth is between Sun and Moon; the entire near side appears lit.
Waxing = increasing lit fraction; waning = decreasing lit fraction.
Left half of the Moon (Northern Hemisphere) is lit, three weeks after New Moon.
Right half of the Moon (Northern Hemisphere) is lit, one week after New Moon.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “New Moon”?
options: Earth is between Sun and Moon; the entire near side appears lit.
Phase when the Moon is between Earth and the Sun; the lit side faces away from Earth.
Time between successive same phases (e.g., New Moon to New Moon): 29.5 days.
Right half of the Moon (Northern Hemisphere) is lit, one week after New Moon.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “First quarter”?
options: Left half of the Moon (Northern Hemisphere) is lit, three weeks after New Moon.
Right half of the Moon (Northern Hemisphere) is lit, one week after New Moon.
Waxing = increasing lit fraction; waning = decreasing lit fraction.
Phase when the Moon is between Earth and the Sun; the lit side faces away from Earth.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Waxing / waning”?
options: Waxing = increasing lit fraction; waning = decreasing lit fraction.
Right half of the Moon (Northern Hemisphere) is lit, one week after New Moon.
Phase when the Moon is between Earth and the Sun; the lit side faces away from Earth.
Time between successive same phases (e.g., New Moon to New Moon): 29.5 days.

mcqs.q: How many days in a synodic month (rounded)?
options: 32 days
28 days
30 days
29 days

numericals.q: How many days in a synodic month (rounded)?

sequence.def: Day 0: Moon between Earth and Sun, unlit face
Days 1-6: sliver grows on the right
Days 8-13: more than half lit, still growing
Day 14-15: fully lit; lunar eclipses possible
